topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Span to Basis

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Span to Basis

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Vector Space
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as an arrow in 2D space. Introduce the concept of 'scaling' and 'adding' vectors as geometric movements (tip-to-tail).
sections.example: A robotic arm moving 2 units East and 3 units North.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Explain that a linear combination is the result of scaling vectors and adding them together. 'Span' is the set of all possible destinations reachable by varying these scale factors.
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors as 'basis' directions: combining them covers the entire 2D plane like a grid.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
sections.content: Introduce linear dependence visually: when a third vector lies on the same line or plane as the others, it adds no new 'reach.' It's redundant information.
sections.example: Three hikers: If hiker A and B are walking on the same trail, hiker C (who is just following them) is linearly dependent.

sections.title: Basis: The Minimalist Framework
sections.content: Define 'Basis' as the smallest set of vectors that span the entire space without any redundancy (linearly independent). This is the 'minimal coordinate system' for the space.
sections.example: Using standard basis vectors (1,0) and (0,1) to describe the location of a pixel on a digital screen.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Wrap up: Span defines the 'reach,' Linear Dependence checks for 'redundancy,' and Basis provides the 'perfect frame.'
sections.example: A GPS system needing exactly 3 satellites (a basis) to pinpoint a coordinate in 3D space.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Vector Space
animations: Create 2D vector 'v' in color #FF5733 appearing from origin.
Label vector 'v' with text "v" in color #FF5733 near the head.
Show scalar multiplication 2*v by scaling vector 'v' to double length.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Linear combinations scale and add vectors.
animations: Visualize the parallelogram sum u+v with dotted lines (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the resultant vector w = u+v in color #FFFF33.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
lecture_lines: A third vector adds no reach.
animations: Show three vectors 'u', 'v', 'w' where w = u + v.
Fade out vector 'w' to demonstrate it is redundant.
Flash vectors 'u' and 'v' to show independence.

storyboard.title: Basis: The Minimalist Framework
lecture_lines: Basis is the minimal span set.
animations: Display a set of basis vectors 'i' (#FF33FF) and 'j' (#33FFFF).
Show vector 'v' as a grid combination of 'i' and 'j'.
Highlight the grid lines to emphasize the spanning property.

storyboard.title: Synthesis and Summary
animations: Assemble vectors, combinations, and basis into a central triangle (#FFFFFF).
Flash each vertex to connect Spanning, Dependence, and Basis.
Fade all components together to show the unified framework.
